raw_case_text:
An 11-week-old female ex-premature infant (corrected gestational age 6 weeks) presented to a peripheral hospital with respiratory distress and a three-day history of cyanotic episodes, following three weeks of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms. The infant was born at 35 weeks' gestation, weighing 2489 g, and did not require resuscitation or respiratory support at birth. The newborn had a 5-day admission to the special care unit for feeding establishment and observation prior to being discharged home well on day 7 of life. The child's mother had received six cycles of R-CHOP for NHL between 17 and 33 weeks of gestation.
The infant was tachypneic and hypoxic, was commenced on high flow nasal cannula support, intravenous (IV) ampicillin and gentamicin, and managed at the peripheral hospital's critical care unit. Over the next two days, respiratory support was escalated to noninvasive ventilation, and antibiotics were changed to IV cefotaxime (D1-D8) and IV azithromycin (D3-D5).
Nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA) was negative for eight respiratory viruses. Respiratory virus detection for influenza A, influenza B, parainfluenza 1, 2, and 3, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and adenovirus was performed using an in-house respiratory virus multiplex real-time RT-PCR assay, while human metapneumovirus (HMPV) was tested with the in-house real-time RT-PCR assay utilising oligonucleotides. Testing for Pneumocystis jirovecii was also requested on the NPA specimen and performed using an in-house real-time RT-PCR assay. A synthetic reference standard was also utilised to enable quantification. Human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) serology was negative. A chest X-ray revealed diffuse bilateral ground glass changes (Figure 1).
As the hypoxic respiratory failure worsened, atypical infections and possible childhood interstitial lung disease (ChILD) were considered and pulse IV methylprednisolone was commenced. The NPA was subsequently positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii DNA at 2.0 x 106 copies/mL. Oral co-trimoxazole 20 mg/kg/day (D4) was commenced and transitioned to IV co-trimoxazole (D8) due to clinical deterioration.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 11-week-old ex-35-week premature female infant born to a mother who received six cycles of R-CHOP chemotherapy during pregnancy presented with acute respiratory distress and a 3-day history of cyanotic episodes following a 3-week upper respiratory prodrome.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Born at 35 weeks' gestation (birth weight 2,489 g, discharged well on day 7 of life) to a mother who had been treated with six cycles of R-CHOP (rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, prednisone) for non-Hodgkin lymphoma between 17 and 33 weeks of gestation, the infant developed 3 weeks of upper respiratory tract infection symptoms followed by 3 days of cyanotic spells and acute respiratory distress at 11 weeks chronological age (6 weeks corrected gestational age).
subjective.past_medical_history: Preterm birth at 35 weeks' gestation (birth weight 2,489 g); in utero exposure to six cycles of maternal R-CHOP immunochemotherapy between 17 and 33 weeks' gestation.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for 3 weeks of upper respiratory symptoms, 3 days of cyanotic episodes, tachypnea, and severe respiratory distress.

objective.physical_examination: Tachypneic and hypoxemic on admission to the peripheral hospital critical care unit, requiring escalation from high-flow nasal cannula to noninvasive ventilation over 48 hours.
objective.routine_investigations: Virological and serological screening: HIV serology negative; nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA) multiplex real-time RT-PCR negative for eight common respiratory viruses (influenza A/B, parainfluenza 1–3, RSV, adenovirus, and human metapneumovirus). Chest X-ray: Diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities.
objective.advanced_workup: Quantitative Pneumocystis jirovecii real-time PCR on nasopharyngeal aspirate (NPA): Strongly positive for Pneumocystis jirovecii DNA at 2.0 x 10^6 copies/mL.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Severe infantile Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PCP; confirmed by quantitative nasopharyngeal aspirate real-time PCR showing 2.0 x 10^6 copies/mL and diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest radiograph) associated with in utero exposure to maternal R-CHOP chemotherapy and secondary combined immunodeficiency. Plan and clinical course: Initially managed with high-flow nasal cannula, noninvasive ventilation, empiric IV ampicillin/gentamicin followed by IV cefotaxime (days 1–8), IV azithromycin (days 3–5), and pulse IV methylprednisolone. Upon quantitative PCR confirmation of P. jirovecii, oral co-trimoxazole (20 mg/kg/day on day 4) was initiated and escalated to intravenous co-trimoxazole on day 8 due to progressive clinical deterioration.
